first_public_release: 1.0.0.2 (1.0.0.1 with the calibration overlay fixed; nothing has been published yet)

physical_validation.1.0.0.1: On the maintainer's Bazzite PC, Baballonia's Eye calibration flashed up in a window and closed, nothing showed in the headset and Baballonia's calibration buttons stayed greyed out, in a VROSTBridge session and with SteamVR alone. coredumpctl: BabbleCalibration.program, SIGSEGV; stack #0 0x0, #1-#3 vrclient.so, #4 OpenVROverlayContainer::draw_overlay (godot-openvr), #5 on_frame_post_draw.
physical_validation.1.0.0.2: not yet tried with SteamVR or the headset

diagnosis: SteamVR's vrclient.so takes an OpenVR overlay's Vulkan texture through extension commands on the program's own VkDevice (external memory and semaphore file descriptors, timeline semaphores).

Godot 4.5 (the calibration program) creates a Vulkan 1.2 instance and enables VK_KHR_external_memory_fd but not VK_KHR_external_semaphore_fd or VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore (RenderingDeviceDriverVulkan, read from its source).

Mesa returns NULL from vkGetDeviceProcAddr for commands of device extensions the program did not enable; on a Vulkan 1.2 device the core timeline commands resolve but their KHR names do not (seen on lavapipe and SwiftShader). Windows drivers return such commands anyway.
The same failure in SteamVR Room Setup on Fedora was analysed by rcannood/steamvr-room-setup-on-fedora (MIT), whose extension list the layer uses; no code was taken from it.
changes: launcher/baballonia.py: the calibration launcher enables the layer for --use-openvr only (VK_ADD_LAYER_PATH, VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS, ahead of the user's; VROSTBRIDGE_VULKAN_LAYER=off leaves it out); prepare_vulkan_layer copies it beside the launcher from the installation's vulkan/ whenever it differs
CMakeLists.txt: the layer built and installed into vulkan/, CTest openvr_texture_layer; packaging refuses a client without it
Version 1.0.0.2 on both programs; documents and release notes

tests.real_calibration_program: Baballonia 1.1.1.0rc6's BabbleCalibration started through the installed launcher with a stand-in vrserver (lavapipe, Xvfb): the launcher switched it to --use-openvr and enabled the layer, which extended Godot's device; OpenVR then found no SteamVR and the program ended (SIGSEGV), as it does without the layer. observations: Mesa (lavapipe here, RADV on the test PC) gives no command for an extension the program did not enable; the KHR names of the timeline commands need VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore even on a Vulkan 1.2 device.
Without SteamVR, Baballonia's calibration in OpenVR mode crashes when OpenVR finds no runtime, with or without the layer.
Chromium's SwiftShader has no X11 surface: Godot falls back to OpenGL there, so the full program ran on lavapipe only.
If a calibration window closes by itself, Baballonia keeps waiting for it with its calibration buttons greyed out until it is restarted (stop and start the session).
not_run: SteamVR taking the overlay's picture with the layer (SteamVR does not run in the build environment)
